rules.quote: Keep responses short and direct.
rules.rule: Keep responses short and direct.

rules.quote: No trailing summaries after tool calls.
rules.rule: Do not add trailing summaries after tool calls.

rules.quote: Lead with the action or finding.
rules.rule: Lead responses with the action taken or the finding.

rules.quote: Only explain when something is non-obvious or needs a decision.
rules.rule: Only explain things when they are non-obvious or require a decision from the user.

rules.quote: Always prepare a git commit statement for review before executing, unless the user says "commit" directly or invokes /commit.
rules.rule: Before executing a git commit, prepare the commit message for review, unless the user says "commit" directly or invokes /commit.

rules.quote: show the proposed commit message as a code block
rules.rule: When changes are ready to commit, show the proposed commit message in a code block.

rules.quote: Only execute when asked.
rules.rule: Only execute a commit when the user asks for it.

rules.quote: When bugs are found while investigating something else, fix them immediately and mention them concisely.
rules.rule: When bugs are found while investigating something else, fix them immediately and mention them concisely.

rules.quote: Always check the agent.log when the user opens it
rules.rule: When the user opens agent.log, read it to diagnose the issue.

rules.quote: Read the tail of the log immediately and report the latest error or status.
rules.rule: When investigating agent.log, read its tail immediately and report the latest error or status.

rules.quote: Delegate downloads, model pulls, and any other human-executable tasks to the user instead of running them via Bash.
rules.rule: Delegate downloads, model pulls, and other human-executable tasks to the user instead of running them via Bash.

rules.quote: give the exact command for the user to run rather than executing it. Do not use Bash for these.
rules.rule: For downloads or installs, give the user the exact command to run instead of executing it, and do not use Bash for these.

rules.quote: Every change — bug fix, config tweak, feature, refactor — must have a corresponding GitHub issue before the work is done.
rules.rule: Before finishing any code or config change (bug fix, config tweak, feature, refactor), ensure a corresponding GitHub issue exists.

rules.quote: Before making any change, check if an issue already exists: `gh issue list --repo vipulbms/crypto-trader-agent`
rules.rule: Before making any change, check whether a GitHub issue already exists for it by running `gh issue list --repo vipulbms/crypto-trader-agent`.

rules.quote: If no issue exists, create one first:
rules.rule: If no GitHub issue exists for the change, create one before making the change.

rules.quote: The issue body must include: **What** (the problem/feature), **Why** (motivation), **How to fix** (proposed approach).
rules.rule: When creating a GitHub issue, include in its body a What section (the problem or feature), a Why section (motivation), and a How to fix section (proposed approach).

rules.quote: Reference the issue in the commit message: `Closes #N` (fully resolved) or `Refs #N` (partial).
rules.rule: Reference the GitHub issue in the commit message using `Closes #N` when the issue is fully resolved, or `Refs #N` when partially resolved.

rules.quote: When closing an issue, leave a comment summarising what was done and which files changed.
rules.rule: When closing a GitHub issue, leave a comment summarising what was done and which files changed.

rules.quote: This applies to ALL change types: bug fixes, config changes, documentation updates, test additions, refactors.
rules.rule: Apply the GitHub issue requirement to all change types, including bug fixes, config changes, documentation updates, test additions, and refactors.

rules.quote: 1. Investigate → confirm root cause
rules.rule: Investigate and confirm the root cause before creating a GitHub issue or making a fix.

rules.quote: 4. Run full test suite — all must pass
rules.rule: Run the full test suite before committing, and ensure all tests pass.

rules.quote: 5. Commit with `Closes #N` in message
rules.rule: Commit changes with `Closes #N` in the commit message.

rules.quote: 6. Confirm issue is closed on GitHub
rules.rule: Confirm the GitHub issue is closed after committing.

rules.quote: All three log files must be wired up in every standalone runtime process (research_analyst.py, data_collector.py, etc.), not just main.py.
rules.rule: Wire up all three log files (agent.log, agent-llm-prompts.log, cycle_decisions.log) in every standalone runtime process such as research_analyst.py and data_collector.py, not only in main.py.

rules.quote: replace `logging.basicConfig()` with a `RotatingFileHandler` on `agent.log`
rules.rule: In a standalone runtime process's main(), replace logging.basicConfig() with a RotatingFileHandler writing to agent.log.

rules.quote: (same `log_dir`/`max_bytes`/`backup_count` from config)
rules.rule: Configure the agent.log RotatingFileHandler using log_dir, max_bytes, and backup_count from config.

rules.quote: Add a `StreamHandler` only when `sys.stdout.isatty()` to avoid duplicate lines in background mode.
rules.rule: Add a StreamHandler to logging only when sys.stdout.isatty() is true, to avoid duplicate lines in background mode.

rules.quote: call `init_llm_logger(log_dir, config)` at startup
rules.rule: Call init_llm_logger(log_dir, config) at process startup.

rules.quote: call `log_llm_interaction(...)` after every `ai_client.chat_with_tools()` response
rules.rule: Call log_llm_interaction(...) after every ai_client.chat_with_tools() response.

rules.quote: Use a module-level `_SESSION_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]`
rules.rule: Define a module-level _SESSION_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] for LLM logging.

rules.quote: a per-module cycle counter
rules.rule: Use a per-module cycle counter for LLM logging.

rules.quote: Pass `prompt_template` to distinguish RAA records from main-agent records
rules.rule: Pass prompt_template to log_llm_interaction so RAA records can be distinguished from main-agent records (e.g., "raa_batch_universe_decision").

rules.quote: call `init_cycle_logger(log_dir, config)` at startup
rules.rule: Call init_cycle_logger(log_dir, config) at process startup.

rules.quote: call `write_raa_cycle_report(cycle_id, duration_ms, candidates, decisions, persistence_data)` at the end of each `run_cycle()`
rules.rule: Call write_raa_cycle_report(cycle_id, duration_ms, candidates, decisions, persistence_data) at the end of each run_cycle().

rules.quote: The RAA record includes `"source": "RAA"` so it can be filtered from main-agent records.
rules.rule: Include "source": "RAA" in RAA cycle records so they can be filtered from main-agent records.

rules.quote: Every code commit must include:
rules.rule: Every code commit must include the required documentation updates (session notes, and README.md or CLAUDE.md where applicable).

rules.quote: new file `docs/sessions/session_YYYY_MM_DDx.md` documenting what changed and why
rules.rule: For every code commit, create a new session notes file at docs/sessions/session_YYYY_MM_DDx.md documenting what changed and why.

rules.quote: README.md** update — if the feature is user-facing or affects trading behavior
rules.rule: Update README.md when the change is user-facing or affects trading behavior.

rules.quote: CLAUDE.md** update — if the feature is architectural or impacts known behaviors
rules.rule: Update CLAUDE.md when the change is architectural or impacts known behaviors.

rules.quote: When using `/commit`, always create a corresponding session note (even for hotfixes)
rules.rule: When using /commit, always create a corresponding session note, even for hotfixes.

rules.quote: Session notes should include: issue #, root cause (if bug), what changed, testing, related sessions
rules.rule: Session notes should include the issue number, root cause (if it is a bug), what changed, testing, and related sessions.

rules.quote: README updates needed for: new personas, trading mechanics, CLI commands, config changes
rules.rule: Update README when adding new personas, changing trading mechanics, changing CLI commands, or changing config.

rules.quote: CLAUDE.md updates needed for: architecture changes, known behaviors, critical design decisions
rules.rule: Update CLAUDE.md when making architecture changes, documenting known behaviors, or recording critical design decisions.

rules.quote: All three should be committed in the same git commit (atomic documentation + code)
rules.rule: Commit session notes, README/CLAUDE.md updates, and code changes together in the same git commit.

rules.quote: All tests — whether written by Claude or Copilot — must be saved in the `tests/` folder
rules.rule: Save all tests, regardless of who writes them, in the `tests/` folder so they can be found, rerun, and extended in future sessions.

rules.quote: Never write test logic as inline `python3 -c "..."` scripts when the test is validating a real feature.
rules.rule: Never write test logic as inline `python3 -c` scripts when validating a real feature; write it to `tests/test_<feature>.py` instead.

rules.quote: Every test function must have a Gherkin-style docstring:
rules.rule: Give every test function a Gherkin-style docstring (Given/When/Then).

rules.quote: When code behaviour changes (e.g. a signal rule is updated), review existing tests in `tests/` and update any that test the changed behaviour.
rules.rule: When code behaviour changes, review existing tests in `tests/` and update any that test the changed behaviour.

rules.quote: Tests should be runnable standalone: `~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python3 tests/test_<feature>.py`
rules.rule: Make tests runnable standalone, executable directly as `~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python3 tests/test_<feature>.py`.

rules.quote: Use this context when making any code or config changes to understand the full system.
rules.rule: When making any code or config change, consult this project context to understand the full system.

rules.quote: `config.yaml` — ALL parameters (no hardcoded values in source)
rules.rule: Keep all parameters in config.yaml; do not hardcode parameter values in source code.

rules.quote: Score weights all in `config.yaml` under `signals:`. Never hardcode them.
rules.rule: Never hardcode signal score weights; keep them in config.yaml under signals:.

rules.quote: `decision_type` values are `BUY`/`SELL`/`HOLD` (not `TRADE_BUY`)
rules.rule: Use only BUY, SELL, or HOLD as decision_type values; never use TRADE_BUY.

rules.quote: Tool execution always uses the signal `pair`, never `tool_args["pair"]`
rules.rule: Execute tools using the signal's pair, never tool_args["pair"], because the LLM hallucinates pair names.

rules.quote: `set_cycle_id()` must be called in `main.py` immediately after `audit.log_cycle()` — before signals are computed
rules.rule: Call set_cycle_id() in main.py immediately after audit.log_cycle() and before signals are computed.

rules.quote: always verify it after any paper_broker.py edit
rules.rule: After any edit to paper_broker.py, verify that PaperBroker.get_balance() still returns total_usd as cash plus open position entry cost.

rules.quote: `paper_broker.py` requires `from datetime import datetime`
rules.rule: Keep `from datetime import datetime` in paper_broker.py.

rules.quote: Always close DB connections AFTER all queries — never before
rules.rule: Close database connections only after all queries have completed; never close them before.

rules.quote: `prompts.py` system prompt must stay aligned with signal scorer weights
rules.rule: Keep the prompts.py system prompt aligned with the signal scorer weights.

rules.quote: never hardcode RSI thresholds as mandatory BUY conditions
rules.rule: Never hardcode RSI thresholds as mandatory BUY conditions in the prompts.py system prompt.

rules.quote: `prompts.py` must use an explicit decision tree (Signal=BUY → propose_buy)
rules.rule: prompts.py must use an explicit decision tree in which Signal=BUY leads to propose_buy.

rules.quote: with an exhaustive list of override conditions
rules.rule: prompts.py must include an exhaustive list of override conditions.

rules.quote: never vague "when in doubt, hold" language
rules.rule: Never use vague "when in doubt, hold" language in prompts.py.

rules.quote: Do NOT raise `bb_min_width_pct` above 0.5%
rules.rule: Do not raise bb_min_width_pct above 0.5%.

rules.quote: never stages .env/data/logs
rules.rule: The /commit skill must never stage .env, data, or logs files.

rules.quote: run after any `risk_manager.py` changes
rules.rule: Run tests/test_circuit_breaker.py after any change to risk_manager.py.

rules.quote: Run after any `signals.py` or `features.py` edit.
rules.rule: Run tests/test_per_pair_params.py after any edit to signals.py or features.py.

rules.quote: keep SKILL.md in sync whenever signal logic or risk rules change
rules.rule: Keep .claude/skills/trading-rules/SKILL.md in sync whenever signal logic or risk rules change.

rules.quote: do not hardcode deepseek-r1 anywhere
rules.rule: Do not hardcode the model name deepseek-r1 anywhere; keep LLM references model-agnostic.

rules.quote: must resolve to 'closed' before SL/TP orders are attached
rules.rule: In live trading, wait for limit orders to resolve to 'closed' before attaching SL/TP orders.

rules.quote: regenerate with /explain skill when multiple modules change
rules.rule: Regenerate docs/codebase.md with the /explain skill when multiple modules change.

rules.quote: surgical edits only, never full rewrite
rules.rule: Make only surgical edits to docs/business_requirements.md; never fully rewrite it.

rules.quote: append new stories or tick completed ones only
rules.rule: In docs/epics_stories_ac.md, only append new stories or tick completed ones.

rules.quote: `RiskManager` requires `db_path` param — injected in `main.py`
rules.rule: Pass the db_path parameter to RiskManager, injected in main.py.

rules.quote: run once to create all epics (E1–E12) and 28 stories
rules.rule: Run scripts/create_github_issues.sh only once.
